subject: West Medford Open Studios 2023 Preview
overview: Organizers of West Medford Open Studios discussed the evolution of the event from a small neighborhood gathering in 1999 to its current outdoor format at Duggar Park. The conversation highlighted the 2023 artist lineup, the impact of the pandemic on logistics, and the volunteer efforts required to sustain the nonprofit arts festival.

items.title: Guest introductions and favorite local dining
items.summary: Tanya Howard and Stephanie Todd-Hunter discussed their backgrounds as local artists and shared their favorite Medford restaurants.

items.title: History and founding of West Medford Open Studios
items.summary: Howard described the 1999 founding of the organization, which began with a small group of neighbors opening their homes and studios to the community.

items.title: Expansion into performing arts
items.summary: The organizers noted the addition of writers' readings, musical performances, and film screenings to the original visual arts focus.

items.title: COVID-19 impact and move to Duggar Park
items.summary: Todd-Hunter recounted the transition to an outdoor festival model at Duggar Park in 2021 after the 2020 event was moved entirely online.

items.title: 2023 event preview and student involvement
items.summary: The 2023 festival will feature 71 artists at Duggar Park and the West Medford Community Center, including installations from Medford High School and MassArt students.

items.title: Funding, nonprofit status, and volunteers
items.summary: The board discussed the challenges of securing cultural council grants and the critical role of volunteers in managing festival logistics.

items.title: Event logistics and artist directories
items.summary: Participants reviewed the schedule for June 24, including the rain date, transit access, and the availability of digital artist portfolios on the organization’s website.
